title: Vietnamese Bun Rieu with Herbes de Provence
description: A sweet, adventurous twist on the classic Vietnamese noodle soup, featuring herbes de Provence and a crispy fried shallot topping.

ingredients.name: Pork blood
ingredients.notes: Halal-friendly, you can omit if not comfortable with blood.

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork blood and fish sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until the blood is lightly browned.
Add the tomato puree, pork fillet, and fish balls. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.
Add the noodles to the pot and cook for 2-3 minutes, until heated through.
Stir in the cheese until melted and gooey.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Garnish with thinly sliced shallots, chopped cilantro, and a sprinkle of herbes de Provence.
Serve hot, with additional fish sauce and lime wedges on the side.
In a separate pan, heat a thin layer of oil over medium heat. Fry the shallots until crispy, about 5-7 minutes, until golden brown.
Drain the fried shallots on paper towels and sprinkle over the soup.
Serve immediately, with a cheese pull on top.
Bun Rieu is traditionally served with a crispy fried shallot topping, but you can omit if you prefer a lighter version.
